sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Why do GDP and per capita income not effectively measure the quality of people's life?
questions.answer: (1) Its major indicator, the GDP is a specific measure of economic welfare that does not take into account important aspects such as leisure time, environmental quality, freedom, social justice, or gender equality. (2) Per capita income is only an average and does not show inequality of income, so it cannot tell whether the benefits of development reach the poor and disadvantaged.

questions.q: What is sustainable development? Give one example.
questions.answer: (1) Sustainable development is defined as ‘development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs’. (2) Example: using solar or wind energy and rainwater harvesting instead of over-using coal and groundwater.

questions.q: Explain any three causes of regional disparities in India.
questions.answer: (1) Industrial growth: The initial distribution of industries in India was determined by the historical process of growth driven primarily by the interests of the British Rulers. The most prominent among such areas are the tribal areas of central and north-eastern India. (2) Geographical — deserts of Rajasthan and hilly terrain of the North-East restrict development; remoteness from national markets. (3) Lack of infrastructure and poor governance — States without roads, power and law and order cannot attract investment or use funds well.

questions.q: Describe the three-pronged strategy adopted for the empowerment of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
questions.answer: (1) Economic incentives such as free education, free books and free uniforms; Different programmes have been initiated such as mid-day meal, supply (ii) Schools for SCs and STs such as Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya and special treatment in Navodaya Vidyalaya, National Talent Search Schemes, Scholarships are also provided. (2) Economic empowerment — loans and support from NSFDC, NSKFDC, NSTFDC, SC/ST Development Corporations and marketing help from TRIFED. (3) The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, and the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 are important.

questions.q: Explain any three measures taken by the government for the economic and social empowerment of women.
questions.answer: (1) Since women comprise the majority of the population below the poverty line, poverty eradication programmes are specifically addressed to their needs and problems. In view of the critical role of women in the agriculture and allied sectors as producers, concentrated efforts are being made to ensure that benefits of training, extension and various programmes reach them in proportion to their numbers. This has played a central role in the process of enhancing women’s participation in public life. (2) Comprehensive support in terms of labour legislation, social security and other support services is provided to women to enable them to participate in various industrial sectors, especially electronics, information technology, food processing, agro industry and textiles. The provision of support services for women, like child care facilities, including crèches at work places and educational institutions, homes for the aged and the disabled are being improved to create an enabling environment and to ensure their full cooperation in social, political and economic life. (3) Equal access to education, health and nutrition and elimination of violence against women; politically, one-third reservation in local bodies.

or.q: What is the role of the National Rural Health Mission? Mention any two other health programmes for women and children.
or.answer: (1) Medical facilities are concentrated in cities, so NRHM was launched to provide accessible, affordable health care in rural areas, reducing the rural–urban gap. (2) Apart from NRHM, Government of India has also launched many programmes related to health of women and children like Janani Suraksha Yojna (JSY), Balika Samridhi Yojna (BSY), and Kishori Shakti Yojna (KSY).

questions.q: Describe any three measures adopted to reduce drop-out rates and improve achievement in schools.
questions.answer: (1) Creating parental awareness and community mobilization; Involvement of community and Panchayati Raj Institutions; (2) Economic incentives such as free education, free books and free uniforms; (3) Improvement in the content and process of schooling; and National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education (Mid-day Meal Scheme).

questions.answer: (1) The Human Development Index (HDI) was developed in 1990 by a group of economists including Dr. It has been used since then by United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in its annual Human Development Report. The basic use of HDI is to measure a country’s level of development. (2) Life expectancy at birth, as an index of population health and longevity Human Development Index (HDI) has three components: a long and healthy life; knowledge and a descent standard of living. (3) Knowledge and education — adult literacy rate and combined gross enrolment ratio. (4) A decent standard of living — GDP per capita at purchasing power parity in US$. India is in the medium category near the bottom — 128 of 177 countries in 2007–08 — showing that high growth has not yet improved quality of life for all.
